mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above its previous 12-month average signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depress consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when wage growth (not observed) is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong commodity price declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a dual deterioration in the labor market, which amplifies consumer weakness and reduces corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases while PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline in triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below its long-run average (last 10 years) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 2%, the combination signals accommodative policy with rising inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 10-year average AND CPIAUCSL > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when GDP growth (not observed) is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above baseline in triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA AND INDPRO > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above baseline in triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).
